### Love Leads with Forgiveness
Author: Trisha Keehn
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/beloved-women/beloved-women-september-10-2020.html
Passage: Luke 23:34
Points:
- Hurt and fear of being taken advantage of often tempt us to hold onto resentment.
- Even amid excruciating agony and injustice, Jesus prioritized forgiveness above all else.
- True Christian love relinquishes personal rights and trusts God to work in hearts.
- Extending forgiveness to offenders demonstrates genuine faith in Christ's way of life.

### What Does Luke 23:43 Mean?
Author: Gabriel N.E. Fluhrer
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/articles/what-does-luke-23-43-mean
Passage: Luke 23:43
Points:
- Eternal salvation is immediate upon death through faith alone, not dependent on personal works.
- Christ extends the promise of paradise individually and exclusively to those who seek Him.
- Heaven is a sure reality guaranteed by Christ's finished work rather than wishful thinking.
- The deepest joy of paradise is unbroken, everlasting fellowship with Jesus Himself.

### Will Graham Devotion: The Criminal on the Cross
Author: Will Graham
Site: Billy Graham Evangelistic Association
URL: https://billygraham.org/articles/will-graham-devotion-the-criminal-on-the-cross
Passage: Luke 23:39-43
Points:
- The dying thief recognized the reality of his own guilt and Christ's complete innocence.
- He understood that the human soul endures beyond bodily death into eternity.
- Completely unable to save himself, he entrusted his soul entirely to Jesus.
- Christ's merciful reply shows His readiness to grant salvation to anyone who calls on Him.

### The Most Unlikely Believer in the Bible
Author: Mark Jones
Site: Desiring God
URL: https://www.desiringgod.org/articles/the-most-unlikely-believer-in-the-bible
Passage: Luke 23:39-43
Points:
- The repentant criminal showed extraordinary faith by believing in a crucified, suffering Savior.
- His heart was transformed in direct answer to Jesus' prayer for forgiveness.
- He displayed deep theological clarity by fearing God, confessing his sin, and honoring Jesus as King.
- Genuine faith does not treat salvation as an afterthought, but embraces Christ as supreme treasure.
